subject: Chemistry
title: Polonium: Curie's Deadly Legacy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Polonium: Curie's Deadly Legacy.

hook.text: Marie Curie named polonium after her homeland Poland—then occupied and erased from the map of Europe.

buildup.text: She discovered it in 1898 while searching for the source of extra radioactivity in pitchblende.

discovery.text: Polonium is 250,000 times more radioactive than uranium. A microgram can be lethal.

twist.text: In 2006, Alexander Litvinenko was assassinated with polonium-210 slipped into his tea in London.

climax.text: Named for a country that didn't officially exist. Now known as one of the deadliest substances on Earth.

punchline.text: Named for a lost country. Lethal in a speck. Curie's dangerous gift.

quiz.question: Why did Marie Curie name the element polonium?
options: To honor her homeland Poland, which was occupied at the time
Because it was found near the North Pole
It was named after a Polish king

details.summary: Polonium was discovered by Marie and Pierre Curie in 1898 and named after Marie's homeland Poland, then under foreign partition. It is millions of times more radioactive than uranium per gram and gained notoriety when polonium-210 was used to assassinate former Russian spy Alexander Litvinenko in.
details.whyItMatters: Polonium demonstrates how radioactive elements discovered through pure science can become tools of both technology and political assassination. It powers spacecraft and satellites through radioisotope thermoelectric generators.
takeaways: Marie Curie named polonium after her occupied homeland Poland as a political statement
Polonium-210 is so radioactive that microgram quantities generate lethal radiation doses
It was used to assassinate Alexander Litvinenko in London in 2006

faq.question: How was polonium-210 used to assassinate Alexander Litvinenko?
faq.answer: Litvinenko was allegedly given tea laced with polonium-210 at a London hotel in 2006. As an alpha emitter, polonium-210 is undetectable by standard radiation detectors. Once ingested, it irradiated his internal organs. He died from acute radiation syndrome three weeks later..

faq.question: What useful applications does polonium have despite its extreme danger?
faq.answer: Polonium-210 generates intense heat from radioactive decay, making it useful in radioisotope thermoelectric generators for space missions where solar panels are impractical. It is also used as a static eliminator in industrial processes..
